findings.finding: The dataset contains sensitive attributes such as age and personal status (sex), which are used in the analysis. There is a risk that these sensitive attributes may affect the fairness of the lending decisions. "Activities or data inputs involving special categories of personal data are prohibited" (Directive (EU) 2023/2225, Article 18(3)-(4)).
findings.recommendation: Review the dataset to ensure that sensitive attributes are either justified for inclusion or excluded from model features.
findings.title: Handling of Sensitive Attributes

findings.finding: The evidence does not clearly indicate whether consumers can obtain a comprehensible explanation of the creditworthiness assessment, express a viewpoint, or request a human review, as required by Directive (EU) 2023/2225, Article 18(8)-(9).
findings.recommendation: Establish procedures ensuring that consumers are informed about their rights and have access to explanations of their creditworthiness assessments.
findings.title: Automated Assessment Explainability Rights

findings.finding: There is no evidence presented to assess whether performance or selection rates diverge across groups defined by sensitive attributes. Consequently, subgroup disparity cannot be ruled out based on the provided information.
findings.recommendation: Implement systematic monitoring to evaluate performance and selection rates across different demographic groups to ensure no significant disparities exist.
findings.title: Potential Subgroup Disparity

findings.finding: The events logged in the audit report do not provide a comprehensive traceable record that aligns with the purpose of the activity as required by Article 12. Although there are recorded events indicating actions taken, the overall integrity and completeness of the log is uncertain. Event sequence 28 indicates the recording of the activity profile, but further details regarding the completeness of actions and decisions are needed.
findings.recommendation: Enhance the logging mechanism to ensure all relevant actions and decisions are documented in a traceable manner aligned with the activity's purpose.
findings.title: Insufficient record-keeping regarding activity's purpose

findings.finding: While the activity profile states that a Lead Data Scientist and Credit Risk Manager may intervene, the evidence does not clearly show the ability of these individuals to effectively override, intervene in, or stop the automated processes at critical decision points. The oversight structure requires further clarity to demonstrate compliance with Article 14.
findings.recommendation: Clearly document the specific mechanisms and processes that allow for human intervention.
findings.title: Unclear human oversight capabilities

findings.finding: The output does not contain sufficient technical documentation that meets the requirements outlined in Article 11 of the EU AI Act. There is no mention of the design, capabilities, limitations, or monitoring of the system being documented and kept up to date. This is necessary for compliance and assessment.
findings.recommendation: Develop and maintain comprehensive technical documentation as per the requirements specified in Article 11.
findings.title: Insufficient evidence of technical documentation
